verifier_review_result.summary: One required functional checker is missing: explicit enforcement of exact one-cycle no-stall latency from accepted input to output valid. Existing value checks can pass without proving the required cycle-accurate latency behavior.

findings.requirement: Acceptance criterion and latency_model require exact one-cycle no-stall latency: with rst_n=1 and out_ready=1 and no prior occupancy, an input transfer at cycle t must produce corresponding out_valid/data at cycle t+1 (not earlier/later).
findings.evidence: Current assertions check output value equality when recv_one returns and protocol stall stability/reset behavior, but there is no cycle-accurate assertion tying an accepted input edge to mandatory out_valid assertion exactly next cycle under no-stall conditions.
findings.recommended_change: Add a TB temporal assertion/checker that, for no-stall setup (out_ready high, empty state), records accepted input on a rising edge and asserts at the next rising edge that out_valid=1 with matching out_sum; also fail if output appears in same cycle or is delayed beyond t+1 for that transaction.
